title: Let anger die down within
odia:
ଚୂନ ରାଗ ପାନେ ମରୁ
ମନ ରାଗ ମନେ ମରୁ।
literal_meaning: Let lime’s sharpness die in the betel; let the mind’s anger die in the mind.
meaning_odia: ଏହି ପାଠରେ ଚୂନର ରାଗ ଅର୍ଥ କଡ଼ାପଣ, ମନର ରାଗ ଅର୍ଥ କ୍ରୋଧ। ଚୂନର କଡ଼ାପଣ ପାନରେ ମରୁ, ମନର କ୍ରୋଧ ମନରେ ଶାନ୍ତ ହେଉ—ଏହି ତୁଳନା ରହିଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ରାଗକୁ ବାହାରେ ଝାଡ଼ିବା ବଦଳରେ ଶାନ୍ତ ହେବାକୁ ଦେବାର କଥା ଏହା। ମୂଳ ଛାପାର ଦୁଇଟି ରଗକୁ ଏଠାରେ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ଅନୁମାନରେ ରାଗ କରାଯାଇଛି।
explanation: The proposed reading turns on two senses of ରାଗ: sharpness in lime and anger in the mind. Each is asked to die away within its own setting. Our editorial reading hears a wish for anger to subside before it is directed outward. Both occurrences of ରାଗ are explicitly conjectural repairs of the upload’s ରଗ.
usage_example: Original imagined example: Before sending an angry reply, someone pauses and recalls the couplet as a wish for the anger to settle first.
cultural_context: The parallel ପାନେ / ମନେ and repeated ମରୁ link the material image to an inner feeling. Lime and betel supply the first setting; the mind supplies the second.
